title: Rolling Down the Valley
summary: How gradient descent finds the bottom of a valley: the slope says which way is downhill, each step moves against it, and a step that is too large overshoots and bounces.

pages.section: Hook: find the bottom without seeing it
pages.say: A point sits on the curve f(x) = x squared, at x = 3. It cannot see the whole valley, only the ground right under it. How does it find the lowest point?

beats.action: is drawn along its length across the plane
grows from a point on the curve, drop line to the x-axis

beats.object: the plane outside a small window around the dot
beats.action: dims to muted, leaving only the curve near the dot bright

beats.object: the bottom of the parabola at x = 0
beats.action: a dashed ring pulses once around the vertex

pages.say: What the point can feel is the slope. For x squared the slope is 2x, so at x = 3 it is 6. A positive slope means the ground rises to the right, so downhill is to the left.

beats.object: a yellow tangent line at the dot
beats.action: grows out from the dot along the curve's direction
is written in the right third, 2x in yellow
ticks to 6 as 2·3 is substituted

beats.object: a yellow arrow along the x-axis
beats.action: grows from the dot pointing right, uphill

beats.object: a white arrow along the x-axis
beats.action: grows from the dot pointing left, opposite the yellow one

pages.say: So take a step against the slope. The new x is the old x minus a step size eta times the slope. With eta = 0.1, that is 3 minus 0.1 times 6, which gives 2.4.

beats.action: slides up into the right third and becomes a minus sign

beats.object: the update rule x ← x − η·f'(x)
beats.action: is written left to right, η in green, f'(x) in yellow
morphs: η becomes 0.1 and f'(x) becomes 6, x becomes 3
morphs into x = 2.4 while the blue dot slides down the curve to x = 2.4

pages.section: Example: repeat until the slope is flat
pages.say: Then do it again. From 2.4 the slope is 4.8, so the next x is 1.92. Each step is smaller, because the ground gets flatter near the bottom. At x = 0 the slope is 0, and the point stops.

beats.action: its yellow tangent line swings to the new, flatter slope
ticks down from 6 to 4.8
slides along the curve to x = 1.92, leaving a muted footprint
takes several more steps, each shorter, footprints bunching up
turns slowly toward horizontal as the dot descends
settles at the vertex, tangent flat, readout reads 0
beats.camera: zoom in on the vertex, then back

pages.section: Mechanism: too big a step overshoots
pages.say: Now make the step size too large: eta = 1.1. From 3 the point jumps right past the bottom to minus 3.6, then back to 4.32. It bounces from side to side, higher each time, and never settles.

beats.object: the green η in the update rule
beats.action: its value ticks from 0.1 up to 1.1
returns to x = 3 on the same parabola
leaps on an arc over the vertex to x = −3.6
leaps back over the vertex to x = 4.32, higher up the wall

beats.object: a dashed zigzag path between the jumps
beats.action: is drawn across the vertex, each segment longer than the last
beats.camera: pull out to show the widening bounce

pages.section: Close: the small step reaches the bottom
pages.say: With a small step, the point goes back to rolling down: from 3, step by step, to the bottom at x = 0. Feel the slope, step against it, and keep the steps small.

beats.object: the step-size readout η beside the parabola
beats.action: ticks back down from 1.1 to 0.1, the zigzag fades to muted
rolls from x = 3 down the curve in shrinking steps to the vertex

beats.object: the update rule x ← x − η·f'(x)
beats.action: is boxed with a blue surround and held
